essence: Śiva alone, possessing spanda, self-established, makes the inner face taste; this hero, lord of the Kula, is victorious. Kṣemarāja's commentary: whose greatness is unmeasured, who measures the world from earth to Sadāśiva in the heart, who displays creation-dissolution plays — he alone, of non-dual nature, endowed with his own autonomy-power, established in his own nature, like an ocean unmoved by world-waves, shines supreme. Recognition (pratyabhijñā) is tasting this spanda in one's own inner face.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta (wonder at Śiva's spanda) with śānta (tranquility of self-established nature)
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is wonder (vismaya) at Śiva's unmeasured greatness (akalitamahimā), resolving into tranquility (śama) — the ocean unmoved by world-waves. Application: Abhinava does not explicitly name a rasa for this verse; the adbhuta/śānta reading is mine.
